exam.title: Microsoft Certified: SQL AI Developer Associate

questions.promptHtml: A team wants to store embedding vectors with transactional order data and query both in one ACID database engine. Which platform choice best fits?

options.label: Azure SQL Database with native vector support
Azure Blob Storage containers with lifecycle rules
Azure Files shares with SMB access

questions.correctLabel: Azure SQL Database with native vector support
questions.rationaleHtml:
Azure SQL Database can keep relational rows and vectors together, so transactional writes and vector lookups stay in one engine.

Reference: Vector search in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Blob and file storage are great for objects, but they do not provide relational joins, ACID OLTP patterns, or native SQL vector querying.

questions.promptHtml: You must find the most semantically similar support article to a user question embedding. Which T-SQL function should you use in the ranking query?

options.label: JSON_VALUE to parse the vector payload
VECTOR_DISTANCE to score embedding similarity
STRING_SPLIT to tokenize question text

questions.correctLabel: VECTOR_DISTANCE to score embedding similarity
questions.rationaleHtml:
VECTOR_DISTANCE computes distance between vectors so you can ORDER BY similarity for nearest-neighbor retrieval.

Reference: VECTOR_DISTANCE (Transact-SQL)
questions.extraHtml: JSON_VALUE and STRING_SPLIT are useful utilities, but they do not compute numeric distance between embeddings.

questions.promptHtml: A chatbot on Azure SQL should reduce hallucinations by grounding answers in approved internal content. Which architecture pattern should you implement?

options.label: Pure prompting with no retrieval layer
Keyword-only lookup with no semantic ranking
RAG that retrieves approved chunks before generation

questions.correctLabel: RAG that retrieves approved chunks before generation
questions.rationaleHtml:
RAG augments model prompts with trusted retrieved context, improving factual grounding and traceability.

Reference: Retrieval-augmented generation overview
questions.extraHtml: Pure prompting cannot cite enterprise facts reliably. Keyword-only lookup often misses semantically relevant passages.

questions.promptHtml: Security requires the app to access Azure OpenAI without embedding API keys in code or config files. What should the app use?

options.label: A managed identity with Microsoft Entra token auth
A shared SQL login stored in appsettings.json
A hard-coded OpenAI key inside source control

questions.correctLabel: A managed identity with Microsoft Entra token auth
questions.rationaleHtml:
Managed identities remove secret handling and allow token-based access controlled by Azure RBAC.

Reference: Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure SQL
questions.extraHtml: Secret-based methods increase rotation and leakage risk. Managed identity is the least-secret operational model.

questions.promptHtml: You need to protect a national ID column so DBAs cannot view plaintext values, while the application can still query with parameterized predicates. Which feature is best?

options.label: Transparent Data Encryption only
Always Encrypted with secure enclaves
Database-level firewall rules

questions.correctLabel: Always Encrypted with secure enclaves
questions.rationaleHtml:
Always Encrypted keeps sensitive data encrypted at rest, in transit, and in use boundaries, with client-side key control.

Reference: Always Encrypted with Azure Key Vault
questions.extraHtml: TDE protects files at rest, not DBA visibility in query results. Firewalls control network entry, not column exposure.

questions.promptHtml: A SaaS app stores many tenants in one database and must ensure each tenant only reads its own rows in every query path. Which control should be primary?

options.label: Separate schemas with naming conventions only
Nightly export jobs per tenant
Row-level security predicates

questions.correctLabel: Row-level security predicates
questions.rationaleHtml:
Row-level security enforces per-row filters in the database engine, independent of app query mistakes.

Reference: Row-level security
questions.extraHtml: Naming conventions are advisory, not enforcement. Export jobs do not secure online transactional reads.

questions.promptHtml: An AI endpoint slowed after a deployment. You need automatic recommendations such as missing indexes and plan regressions from Azure SQL. Which feature should you check first?

options.label: Intelligent Insights in Azure SQL
Azure DevOps pull request comments
Storage account lifecycle reports

questions.correctLabel: Intelligent Insights in Azure SQL
questions.rationaleHtml:
Intelligent Insights analyzes telemetry for regressions and surfaces actionable performance diagnostics.

Reference: Intelligent Insights
questions.extraHtml: DevOps comments and storage lifecycle reports are useful elsewhere but do not analyze SQL runtime behavior.

questions.promptHtml: A vector-enabled query became slower because the optimizer picked a bad plan after stats drift. Which built-in capability can force a known good plan safely?

options.label: Auto-failover groups
Query Store plan forcing
Elastic job schedules

questions.correctLabel: Query Store plan forcing
questions.rationaleHtml:
Query Store tracks plan history and supports forcing a stable plan when regressions occur.

Reference: Query Store in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Failover groups provide DR, and elastic jobs orchestrate tasks; neither controls query plan selection.

questions.promptHtml: Your retrieval query needs lexical precision for exact product terms plus semantic relevance from embeddings. Which design is best?

options.label: Use only VECTOR_DISTANCE and remove all text filtering
Use only LIKE with wildcard text scans
Combine full-text filtering with vector similarity ranking

questions.correctLabel: Combine full-text filtering with vector similarity ranking
questions.rationaleHtml:
Hybrid retrieval pairs lexical recall/precision with semantic ranking for stronger answer quality.

Reference: Full-text search
questions.extraHtml: Vector-only can miss exact constraints; LIKE-only often lacks semantic understanding and scale efficiency.

questions.promptHtml: A product owner asks how to lower token cost in the RAG pipeline without reducing answer quality too much. Which step should you optimize first?

options.label: Chunk and retrieve only top relevant passages
Send entire source documents each prompt
Duplicate every chunk to increase recall

questions.correctLabel: Chunk and retrieve only top relevant passages
questions.rationaleHtml:
Selecting smaller, relevant context lowers token usage while preserving grounding quality.

Reference: Retrieval-augmented generation overview
questions.extraHtml: Sending full documents and duplicates increases cost and may reduce model focus.

questions.promptHtml: You ingest source documents as JSON and must project specific fields into relational columns before embedding. Which SQL capability is most appropriate?

options.label: Spatial indexes with geography type
OPENJSON with explicit schema mapping
SQL Server Agent proxy accounts

questions.correctLabel: OPENJSON with explicit schema mapping
questions.rationaleHtml:
OPENJSON can shred JSON payloads into typed columns for downstream joins and embedding workflows.

Reference: JSON data in SQL Server and Azure SQL
questions.extraHtml: Spatial indexes and Agent proxies do not transform JSON payload structure into relational columns.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants the assistant to cite where each generated statement came from. Which metadata practice should you apply during chunk storage?

options.label: Store only raw chunk text with no identifiers
Store chunk text plus source URI and offsets
Store only embeddings and discard original text

questions.correctLabel: Store chunk text plus source URI and offsets
questions.rationaleHtml:
Keeping source metadata with chunks enables citation and traceability in generated answers.

Reference: Retrieval-augmented generation overview
questions.extraHtml: Text without provenance cannot support citations. Embeddings alone lose human-readable evidence.

questions.promptHtml: You must provide cross-region continuity for an AI-enabled transactional app using Azure SQL with low manual failover effort. What should you configure?

options.label: Auto-failover groups between paired regions
BACPAC export once per month
Client retry loops without secondary database

questions.correctLabel: Auto-failover groups between paired regions
questions.rationaleHtml:
Auto-failover groups provide managed geo-replication and endpoint redirection for continuity.

Reference: Auto-failover groups
questions.extraHtml: Monthly exports are for backup portability, not near-continuous service. Retries cannot recover from region-wide database loss alone.

questions.promptHtml: Legal asks for recovery to any point in the last 14 days after accidental data deletion. Which Azure SQL capability directly supports this?

options.label: Automatic tuning recommendations
Point-in-time restore from automated backups
Static data masking rules

questions.correctLabel: Point-in-time restore from automated backups
questions.rationaleHtml:
Point-in-time restore lets you recover a database to a selected timestamp within retention.

Reference: Recover Azure SQL Database from backups
questions.extraHtml: Automatic tuning is for performance, and masking does not restore deleted data.

questions.promptHtml: A development team keeps regenerating embeddings for unchanged documents, causing needless cost and latency. What is the best fix?

options.label: Rotate SQL admin passwords weekly
Cache embeddings and re-embed only changed content
Increase DTU/CPU tier permanently

questions.correctLabel: Cache embeddings and re-embed only changed content
questions.rationaleHtml:
Change detection with embedding reuse avoids redundant model calls and lowers both latency and spend.

Reference: Embeddings with Azure OpenAI
questions.extraHtml: Password rotation is unrelated, and scaling compute does not remove duplicate embedding requests.

questions.promptHtml: You need to minimize SQL permissions for the AI app that only reads chunks and writes chat logs. Which approach follows least privilege?

options.label: Grant db_owner to simplify onboarding
Grant EXECUTE/SELECT/INSERT only on required objects
Use server admin for all production calls

questions.correctLabel: Grant EXECUTE/SELECT/INSERT only on required objects
questions.rationaleHtml:
Object-scoped permissions provide required access without broad administrative rights.

Reference: Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure SQL
questions.extraHtml: db_owner and server admin exceed the app’s functional need and increase blast radius.

questions.promptHtml: A retrieval query orders by VECTOR_DISTANCE but returns inconsistent relevance because vector dimensions differ between rows. What should you enforce?

options.label: A fixed embedding model and consistent vector dimensions
A random model per microservice deployment
A mix of multilingual and monolingual dimensions

questions.correctLabel: A fixed embedding model and consistent vector dimensions
questions.rationaleHtml:
Distance math assumes comparable vectors; consistent dimensions and model family are required for meaningful similarity.

Reference: Embeddings with Azure OpenAI
questions.extraHtml: Mixing dimensions breaks comparability and causes invalid or low-quality ranking behavior.

questions.promptHtml: You need to protect sensitive terms in logs generated from assistant prompts and completions. Which practice is most appropriate?

options.label: Disable all monitoring permanently
Apply data classification and mask/redact before log persistence
Store raw prompts indefinitely for easier debugging

questions.correctLabel: Apply data classification and mask/redact before log persistence
questions.rationaleHtml:
Redaction and classification reduce exposure while preserving operational insight.

Reference: JSON data in SQL Server and Azure SQL
questions.extraHtml: No monitoring hurts operations, while raw indefinite storage raises privacy and compliance risk.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants to test retrieval quality before production by measuring whether relevant chunks appear in top-k results. Which evaluation is most useful?

options.label: Only track VM CPU usage
Only track number of SQL logins
Use relevance metrics like precision@k and recall@k

questions.correctLabel: Use relevance metrics like precision@k and recall@k
questions.rationaleHtml:
Retrieval metrics directly measure whether the system returns useful context for generation.

Reference: Retrieval-augmented generation overview
questions.extraHtml: Infrastructure metrics help capacity planning but do not prove retrieval relevance quality.

questions.promptHtml: You need to improve semantic recall for long policy PDFs. Which preprocessing step is usually most effective?

options.label: Split text into coherent chunks before embedding
Embed the full 400-page document as one vector
Remove all headings and section boundaries

questions.correctLabel: Split text into coherent chunks before embedding
questions.rationaleHtml:
Chunking preserves local meaning and improves nearest-neighbor retrieval granularity.

Reference: Retrieval-augmented generation overview
questions.extraHtml: Single-vector whole documents lose detail; removing structure can reduce contextual quality.

questions.promptHtml: A database is encrypted with TDE, but auditors still report that privileged users can view sensitive query results. What additional control is needed?

options.label: Geo-backups with longer retention
Always Encrypted for sensitive columns
Larger compute tier for the database

questions.correctLabel: Always Encrypted for sensitive columns
questions.rationaleHtml:
TDE secures storage media, while Always Encrypted protects sensitive values from plaintext exposure in query results.

Reference: Always Encrypted with Azure Key Vault
questions.extraHtml: Backups and compute sizing do not address data visibility at query time.

questions.promptHtml: A product catalog chatbot needs deterministic filtering by brand and region before semantic ranking. Which query pattern should you prefer?

options.label: Apply structured WHERE filters then vector similarity order
Run vector similarity first and filter later in app code
Use random sampling to reduce candidate rows

questions.correctLabel: Apply structured WHERE filters then vector similarity order
questions.rationaleHtml:
Database-side structured filters reduce candidate set early and keep retrieval aligned with hard constraints.

Reference: Vector search in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Late filtering and random sampling can exclude relevant rows or waste compute.

questions.promptHtml: Operations wants automatic remediation when index recommendations repeatedly improve AI query latency. Which setting should you enable?

options.label: SQL auditing to Log Analytics only
Automatic index tuning in Azure SQL
Geo-replication seeding diagnostics

questions.correctLabel: Automatic index tuning in Azure SQL
questions.rationaleHtml:
Automatic tuning can create/drop indexes based on observed workload impact and validation.

Reference: Automatic tuning in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Auditing and replication diagnostics are operationally useful but do not tune indexes automatically.

questions.promptHtml: An assistant must answer only from approved HR policies and refuse unsupported questions. What is the best guardrail?

options.label: Allow model answers from general pretraining knowledge
Prompt with policy context and enforce refusal when retrieval is empty
Disable retrieval to reduce latency

questions.correctLabel: Prompt with policy context and enforce refusal when retrieval is empty
questions.rationaleHtml:
Grounding plus explicit refusal logic prevents fabricated answers outside approved sources.

Reference: Retrieval-augmented generation overview
questions.extraHtml: General-pretraining-only responses and disabled retrieval increase hallucination and compliance risk.

questions.promptHtml: You need to rotate encryption keys for client-side protected columns with minimal downtime. Which key architecture helps most?

options.label: Store keys only in local config files
Use column master keys in Azure Key Vault
Use SQL login passwords as encryption keys

questions.correctLabel: Use column master keys in Azure Key Vault
questions.rationaleHtml:
Azure Key Vault-backed CMKs support centralized key governance and operational rotation workflows.

Reference: Always Encrypted with Azure Key Vault
questions.extraHtml: Local files and SQL passwords are weaker key-governance patterns for regulated data.

questions.promptHtml: A retrieval pipeline pulls duplicate chunks from mirrored sources, causing repetitive answers. Which step should you add?

options.label: De-duplicate content with stable chunk hashes before embedding
Increase prompt temperature to 1.0
Disable source metadata collection

questions.correctLabel: De-duplicate content with stable chunk hashes before embedding
questions.rationaleHtml:
Hash-based deduplication removes repeated context and improves response clarity and token efficiency.

Reference: Retrieval-augmented generation overview
questions.extraHtml: Temperature tuning and metadata removal do not eliminate duplicated source content.

questions.promptHtml: Your team must expose SQL data to a model while preventing direct table access from the app. Which interface pattern is best?

options.label: Grant table SELECT on every schema
Use parameterized stored procedures for approved access paths
Allow ad hoc dynamic SQL from user prompts

questions.correctLabel: Use parameterized stored procedures for approved access paths
questions.rationaleHtml:
Stored procedures encapsulate business logic and narrow the execution surface for AI-driven requests.

Reference: Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure SQL
questions.extraHtml: Broad table access and dynamic SQL increase injection and overexposure risks.

questions.promptHtml: A multilingual assistant uses one embedding model for English and another for French in the same search column. Retrieval quality drops. What is the main issue?

options.label: Autoscaling is disabled on the SQL server
Different embedding spaces are mixed in one similarity index
Query Store capture mode is set to AUTO

questions.correctLabel: Different embedding spaces are mixed in one similarity index
questions.rationaleHtml:
Vectors from different embedding spaces are not directly comparable, so distance rankings become unreliable.

Reference: Embeddings with Azure OpenAI
questions.extraHtml: Autoscaling and Query Store settings are unrelated to embedding-space compatibility.

questions.promptHtml: You need observability for AI query latency by stage (retrieval vs generation). What telemetry design is best?

options.label: Emit correlated trace IDs with per-stage duration metrics
Log only total request time with no stage detail
Record diagnostics only during major incidents

questions.correctLabel: Emit correlated trace IDs with per-stage duration metrics
questions.rationaleHtml:
Correlated stage-level telemetry isolates bottlenecks and supports reliable SLO tuning.

Reference: Intelligent Insights
questions.extraHtml: Single totals and ad hoc incident logging hide where latency is introduced.

questions.promptHtml: A team uses direct string concatenation to build SQL from user prompts. Which remediation is most important?

options.label: Increase transaction log file size
Use parameterized queries or stored procedure parameters
Enable weekly full backups

questions.correctLabel: Use parameterized queries or stored procedure parameters
questions.rationaleHtml:
Parameterized execution prevents SQL injection and improves plan reuse stability.

Reference: Query Store in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Log sizing and backup cadence do not prevent injection flaws.

questions.promptHtml: A workload has bursty daytime usage and many small tenants. Cost must stay predictable while isolating noisy neighbors reasonably well. Which compute model is best?

options.label: Separate provisioned database for every tenant always
Single shared database with no workload controls
Elastic pools for grouped databases with shared resources

questions.correctLabel: Elastic pools for grouped databases with shared resources
questions.rationaleHtml:
Elastic pools smooth burst patterns across many databases and control cost while preserving database-level isolation.

Reference: Automatic tuning in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Dedicated databases for all tenants can be expensive; one fully shared database may weaken isolation and tuning flexibility.

questions.promptHtml: You must keep generated SQL plans stable during rollout of a new retrieval feature and compare before/after regressions. Which feature should you rely on?

options.label: Query Store historical plan/runtime capture
Azure Policy initiative assignments
Database copy export to bacpac

questions.correctLabel: Query Store historical plan/runtime capture
questions.rationaleHtml:
Query Store provides per-query history and supports controlled plan analysis during feature rollout.

Reference: Query Store in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Policy and export tools do not provide runtime plan history for regression comparison.

questions.promptHtml: A chat assistant writes conversation history to SQL. You need to avoid unbounded table growth while preserving recent context. Which design is best?

options.label: Keep every message forever in one hot table
Use retention/archival policy with recent-window queries
Delete all history after each response

questions.correctLabel: Use retention/archival policy with recent-window queries
questions.rationaleHtml:
Retention plus archival controls storage growth while keeping practical conversational context.

Reference: JSON data in SQL Server and Azure SQL
questions.extraHtml: Keeping everything forever increases cost; deleting everything removes continuity.

questions.promptHtml: A model should answer with the newest policy text immediately after publication. Which indexing strategy helps most?

options.label: Rebuild embeddings once per quarter
Wait for nightly full reload only
Trigger incremental embedding updates on content change events

questions.correctLabel: Trigger incremental embedding updates on content change events
questions.rationaleHtml:
Event-driven incremental updates reduce staleness and keep retrieval aligned to latest approved content.

Reference: Embeddings with Azure OpenAI
questions.extraHtml: Quarterly or nightly-only refresh may leave stale answers for long periods.

questions.promptHtml: You need to restrict which principals can run high-cost vector search procedures in production. What should you implement?

options.label: Dedicated database roles with EXECUTE grants on those procedures
Grant public role execute so every login can test
Rely on naming conventions in procedure names

questions.correctLabel: Dedicated database roles with EXECUTE grants on those procedures
questions.rationaleHtml:
Role-based EXECUTE permissions enforce controlled access to expensive or sensitive operations.

Reference: Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure SQL
questions.extraHtml: Public grants and naming conventions do not provide least-privilege enforcement.

questions.promptHtml: A question requires exact match on SKU code and semantic match on description text. Which result ordering strategy is best?

options.label: Sort purely by creation date
Filter by SKU first, then rank remaining rows by vector distance
Rank entire table by vector distance and ignore SKU

questions.correctLabel: Filter by SKU first, then rank remaining rows by vector distance
questions.rationaleHtml:
Apply hard identifiers first, then semantic ranking for contextual relevance within valid candidates.

Reference: Vector search in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Date sort and unfiltered vector ranking can return wrong SKUs despite semantic similarity.

questions.promptHtml: Compliance requires proving who changed prompt templates stored in SQL and when. Which capability is most appropriate?

options.label: Enable SQL auditing for data and schema change events
Rely on app team memory during incident review
Disable change tracking to reduce overhead

questions.correctLabel: Enable SQL auditing for data and schema change events
questions.rationaleHtml:
Auditing provides immutable event trails for accountability and compliance investigations.

Reference: Intelligent Insights
questions.extraHtml: Informal memory and disabled tracking cannot satisfy evidentiary requirements.

questions.promptHtml: After adding vector columns, update latency increased due to heavier write payloads. Which mitigation is best before scaling hardware?

options.label: Move all writes to a read-only replica
Profile write path and optimize indexing strategy
Disable transaction commits during peak hours

questions.correctLabel: Profile write path and optimize indexing strategy
questions.rationaleHtml:
Measure write hotspots and adjust index/selectivity strategy before costly scale-up decisions.

Reference: Automatic tuning in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Read-only replicas cannot accept writes, and disabling commits is not a valid production strategy.

questions.promptHtml: A deployment pipeline must promote schema changes and retrieval procedures safely across dev/test/prod. Which approach is recommended?

options.label: Manual SSMS edits directly in production
Database project and CI/CD release gates
Ad hoc scripts pasted from chat logs

questions.correctLabel: Database project and CI/CD release gates
questions.rationaleHtml:
Database projects plus gated CI/CD provide repeatable, reviewable, environment-safe deployments.

Reference: Query Store in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Manual or ad hoc script methods create drift and weak change control.

questions.promptHtml: You need to reduce hallucinations when retrieval returns low-similarity matches. Which runtime rule is best?

options.label: Set a similarity threshold and return "insufficient context" below it
Always force the model to answer anyway
Increase max tokens so the model can improvise

questions.correctLabel: Set a similarity threshold and return "insufficient context" below it
questions.rationaleHtml:
Threshold-based refusal is a practical guardrail when retrieved evidence is weak.

Reference: Retrieval-augmented generation overview
questions.extraHtml: Forcing answers and improvisation increase unsupported claims.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants one connection method for SQL and Azure OpenAI using Entra identities from Azure-hosted workloads. Which approach fits?

options.label: Shared SQL authentication and OpenAI API key files
Managed identity with token-based auth for both services
Anonymous public access with firewall IP allowlists

questions.correctLabel: Managed identity with token-based auth for both services
questions.rationaleHtml:
Managed identity enables secretless, centrally governed identity flows across Azure services.

Reference: Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure SQL
questions.extraHtml: Shared passwords/keys and anonymous access weaken security posture and governance.

questions.promptHtml: Retrieval quality is low because chunks exceed model context and split mid-sentence unpredictably. What preprocessing change helps most?

options.label: Use semantically aware chunk sizes with overlap
Disable punctuation before chunking
Store one chunk per entire document

questions.correctLabel: Use semantically aware chunk sizes with overlap
questions.rationaleHtml:
Meaningful chunk boundaries and overlap preserve context continuity for better retrieval.

Reference: Retrieval-augmented generation overview
questions.extraHtml: Punctuation stripping and document-wide chunks usually degrade semantic retrieval quality.

questions.promptHtml: You must analyze top failing AI queries and quickly identify whether failure came from retrieval or generation. Which schema design best supports this?

options.label: Separate event tables for retrieval metrics and generation outcomes keyed by request ID
Single text column storing opaque blobs only
No persistent telemetry, only console output

questions.correctLabel: Separate event tables for retrieval metrics and generation outcomes keyed by request ID
questions.rationaleHtml:
Normalized event telemetry with shared request IDs supports root-cause analysis and trend reporting.

Reference: Intelligent Insights
questions.extraHtml: Opaque blobs and transient console logs hinder systematic troubleshooting.

questions.promptHtml: A retrieval table has frequent inserts and similarity reads. Which index strategy is generally safer to start with?

options.label: Create many overlapping indexes immediately
Start with minimal necessary indexes and measure
Avoid every index including primary keys

questions.correctLabel: Start with minimal necessary indexes and measure
questions.rationaleHtml:
A measured minimal-index baseline avoids write amplification and allows evidence-based tuning.

Reference: Automatic tuning in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Too many indexes slow writes; no indexes hurts lookup and integrity performance.

questions.promptHtml: You need to isolate customer data per region for legal residency while keeping one application codebase. Which approach is best?

options.label: Single global database with region column only
One database per residency boundary with routing logic
Weekly exports to regional storage accounts only

questions.correctLabel: One database per residency boundary with routing logic
questions.rationaleHtml:
Regional database boundaries enforce residency at storage/compute level while app routing preserves shared code.

Reference: Auto-failover groups
questions.extraHtml: A single global store may violate residency controls; exports alone do not serve operational workloads.

questions.promptHtml: A team must migrate legacy FAQ text into a SQL-backed RAG system quickly while preserving source references. What should they do first?

options.label: Define ingestion mapping for text, metadata, and source links
Tune failover group policy before ingestion
Increase backup retention to maximum

questions.correctLabel: Define ingestion mapping for text, metadata, and source links
questions.rationaleHtml:
A clear ingestion schema ensures each chunk carries retrievable content plus citation metadata from day one.

Reference: JSON data in SQL Server and Azure SQL
questions.extraHtml: Failover and backup settings are important but not the first step for content migration quality.

questions.promptHtml: During load testing, generation calls are fast but retrieval SQL is slow. Which action is most targeted?

options.label: Increase model max output tokens
Analyze execution plans and missing-index signals
Rotate OpenAI deployment names

questions.correctLabel: Analyze execution plans and missing-index signals
questions.rationaleHtml:
SQL plan analysis and indexing diagnostics directly target retrieval-stage bottlenecks.

Reference: Query Store in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Token limits and deployment naming do not optimize SQL retrieval performance.

questions.promptHtml: You need to limit blast radius if an app identity is compromised. Which architecture helps most?

options.label: One shared identity for every environment
Use separate managed identities per environment and role
Grant contributor at subscription scope to app identity

questions.correctLabel: Use separate managed identities per environment and role
questions.rationaleHtml:
Scoped identities per environment/role constrain privilege and reduce cross-environment impact.

Reference: Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure SQL
questions.extraHtml: Shared broad identities increase lateral movement and impact severity.

questions.promptHtml: A retrieval procedure accepts user-entered filters for category and price range. How should input be handled?

options.label: Validate and parameterize all user inputs before SQL execution
Concatenate raw input directly into dynamic SQL
Trust UI validation only and skip server checks

questions.correctLabel: Validate and parameterize all user inputs before SQL execution
questions.rationaleHtml:
Server-side validation plus parameterization defends against injection and malformed query behavior.

Reference: Query Store in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Client-only validation and raw concatenation are insufficient security controls.

questions.promptHtml: Business users need predictable monthly cost for a moderate AI workload with occasional spikes. Which sizing approach is best initially?

options.label: Serverless only with no min/max controls
Provisioned tier with monitored right-sizing and scheduled review
Always choose highest tier to avoid all risk

questions.correctLabel: Provisioned tier with monitored right-sizing and scheduled review
questions.rationaleHtml:
A right-sized provisioned baseline with review cadence balances predictability and performance risk.

Reference: Automatic tuning in Azure SQL Database
questions.extraHtml: Unbounded serverless settings or permanent overprovisioning can create cost surprises.
